verdict.rationale: Otter's MCP server is documented as OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions, so an AI assistant can only access meetings the user explicitly authorizes. That is a first-party, scoped grant of access for an agent. However, the evidence comes from a single marketing blog line, and nothing documents scoping for the Public API, so depth is unproven. Missing for 10: documented scope definitions or permission granularity, scoped API keys or tokens for the Public API, credential revocation and expiry controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize
